# Umbra Unit Frames

**Your game. Front and center.**

![World of Warcraft · Unit Frames](https://img.shields.io/badge/World_of_Warcraft-Unit_Frames-75DCC4?style=flat-square&labelColor=15191F)
![Clients · Retail, Forever & Classic](https://img.shields.io/badge/Clients-Retail%2C_Forever_%26_Classic-C9B888?style=flat-square&labelColor=15191F)
[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames?style=flat-square&label=release&color=75DCC4&labelColor=15191F)](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/releases/latest)

---

**Umbra preserves the idea, not every old design decision.**

A project for modern, readable unit frames in World of Warcraft Retail, WoW: Forever and the Classic clients — Mists of Pandaria, the Anniversary realms and Classic Era. Inspired by ShadowedUnitFrames, with a visual identity of its own: class-colored edges, rectangular character portraits beside the bars, and information right where you need it.

[The idea](#the-idea) · [Design principles](#design-principles) · [The frames](#the-frames) · [Using it](#using-it) · [Installing](#installing) · [Supported clients](#supported-clients) · [Contributing](#contributing)

> **Where it stands.** All six design principles are implemented, and every frame in [the table below](#the-frames) that is not marked otherwise. Everything is set in a small options window or through `/uuf`, which do the same, and Clique is not supported. Which version is current, the release badge above says; the [changelog](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) says what each one settled.

---

## The idea

Your character, your target, and your group should be the focus. The interface should help you understand their status — not compete for your attention.

Umbra brings together compact unit frames, a clear information hierarchy, and restrained styling. Rather than replacing the entire user interface, it stays with the unit frames: player, target, pet, target of target, the boss column and the party column.

> **Familiar to use. Distinct by design.**

### Why “Umbra”?

*Umbra* refers to the [dark inner region of a shadow](https://science.nasa.gov/moon/eclipses/). The name acknowledges the project's visual inspiration without simply repeating “Shadowed.”

It also captures the thinking behind the project: **The interface steps back. Your game stays in focus.**

## Design principles

Color, shape, and placement should make different kinds of information easy to distinguish. These six principles define Umbra's visual direction, and all six are implemented.

| Principle | Approach and purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Class color at the edge** | A **3-pixel edge** and the character's name carry the class color. The health bar stays **neutral green** by default, and `/uuf health class` gives it the unit's color as well for anyone who would rather have it there. Class identity and health each have a distinct visual role. |
| **A dedicated portrait column** | A narrow, **rectangular character portrait** sits to the left of the name and bars—including on the target frame. Subtle class tinting replaces circular medallions, glowing portrait rings, and images behind the numbers. The tint lies on the column's ground, behind the model, so no class color is laid over the face. |
| **Resources as a hairline** | Mana, energy, and rage use a thin line rather than a second dominant bar. Health remains the primary information. |
| **Auras with an underline** | A slim colored line beneath each icon replaces a prominent full border. Personal and important effects stay easy to identify without cluttering the grid. |
| **Distinct shields and healing** | Hatching indicates absorbs; a light, translucent segment represents incoming healing. Both stay clearly distinguishable from current health. |
| **Range through fading** | Out-of-range units fade together with their portraits. Class color and character identity remain intact rather than being replaced by a grayscale filter. |

**Accent color belongs to the interface. Class color belongs to the unit. The health bar belongs to health.**

![Five health bars showing plain health, incoming healing as a ghosted segment, a hatched damage absorb, a heal absorb eating backwards into health, and the bar carrying the unit's own class color; beside them the five colors an aura underline takes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/bar-states.svg)

**A theme changes the interface, never the unit.** `/uuf theme` swaps the colors around a unit — the plates and their border, the text, the accent, the cast bar, a window's title — for another set, and leaves the health bar, incoming healing, the absorbs, the class and reaction colors, the resources and the line under a debuff as they are. So *accent color belongs to the interface* holds whichever theme is on. The one besides Umbra's own is [Forever's](#wow-forever).

## The frames

Every frame shares the same anatomy — the portrait column, class color at the edge, the name, a health bar and the power hairline — and is then cut down to what it is for. Names are set in a font family the way Blizzard's own labels are, one file per alphabet, so Cyrillic, Korean and Chinese names draw as well as Latin ones.

![The player frame at twice its size, with every part labeled: the three-pixel class edge, the portrait column, name and power value, health bar, power hairline, class power row and cast bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/frame-anatomy.svg)

> The sheets on this page are **drawings, not screenshots**. `tools/mockups.py` redraws the frames from the same metrics `Core/Defaults.lua` lays them out with, deriving the heights and offsets rather than copying them, so what they can show is geometry and color. The fonts, the spell art in an icon and the portrait models belong to the client and stand in here.

| Frame | What it carries |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Player** | Cast bar, class power row, power value, level, 16 buff and 8 debuff slots. The pet hangs off it and takes a place in its stack. In an inn or a city the client's Z's rise in the portrait's top right corner, out of a fight. |
| **Target** | Cast bar, power value, level, 8 buff and 16 debuff slots — the other way round, because what you have put on the target is the reason to look at it. The level reads in the client's difficulty color, with `+` for an elite and `??` for a unit too far above you, and the health bar turns gray when the kill would be worth nothing: tapped by somebody else, or too far below you. |
| **Pet** | The shared width, so it lines up, but shorter: no cast bar, no aura rows. Its level stands where the player's does. A hunter's pet shows whether it is happy, content or unhappy in the color of its edge and its portrait's ground — green, yellow, red — on WoW: Forever, the Anniversary realms and Classic Era, in place of the reaction color, which on your own pet never changes; pointing at the frame adds the game's own lines for it, the diet among them. |
| **Target of target** | One question — is it on the tank or on me — and cut like the pet. |
| **Boss** | As many as the client has (`MAX_BOSS_FRAMES`), identical to one another, each keeping its cast bar. No aura rows: five stacked frames with rows between them would be a wall. |
| **Party** | A column on the client's own secure group header, so the client creates the children, assigns their units and re-sorts them — in combat as well as out of it. Cast bar, power value, level, one row of debuffs at 14 pixels, the role each member signed up as, and range fading. On WoW: Forever since its release; its beta could not build one — see [Supported clients](#supported-clients). |
| **Raid** | Not yet, and not next. Blizzard's own raid frames do the job, class coloring included; the header carries these whenever they are wanted. |

The level stands in a plate across the foot of the portrait, so the name keeps its whole width; `/uuf level` moves it in front of the name or takes it away. On a scaled unit it is the level you fight it at — the Classic clients do not scale, and show the plain one.

A raid marker — the skull, the cross and the six others the game's menu puts on a unit — stands in the portrait's top left corner, on every frame and inside it, in the game's own art: so the boss column shows the kill order, and the target's target which of the marked it is. On Retail and WoW: Forever the game documents the marker as a value it may hide, and where it does, the frame shows nothing rather than an error; `/uuf dev check` says what the game answered.

There is deliberately **no focus frame**. One was built and taken out again, because a frame that never fills is a frame in the way. It costs a config entry and a point per layout set to put back.

![The party column: four members, each with a role icon left of the name, a cast bar and a row of small debuffs, the tank carrying a square raid marker in the portrait's corner, the fourth faded with its moon because it is out of range](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/party-column.svg)

## Using it

Two **layout sets** decide where everything goes, and each set remembers its own dragged positions. A set decides three things at once, because they only hold together as a set: where the frames sit, which side of a frame each aura row hangs on, and whether the pet sits above the player or below it.

**`modern`** — the default, and the arrangement Dragonflight introduced. Player and target meet in the lower third, buffs above them, the pet under the cast bar and the debuffs under the pet. The party column goes to the left edge, centered on it.

![The modern set on a screen: player and target in the lower third with aura rows above and below, the party column centered on the left edge, the boss column on the right; the target and the first boss carry a skull, the second boss a cross](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/layout-modern.svg)

**`classic`** — where the player frame lived before Dragonflight. The pet is the topmost thing in the stack, so both aura rows hang below, and the party column hangs under the player's whole block rather than under the frame.

![The classic set on a screen: player and target stacked into the top left with the pet above them and both aura rows below, the party column under the player's block, the boss column on the right; the target and the first boss carry a skull, the second boss a cross](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/layout-classic.svg)

The boss column is the same in both: the right edge, centered, as many frames as the client has. It is not part of the arrangement you chose — it is something the fight brings.

**Debuffs over the buffs.** Either set can draw the debuff row over the buff row instead, with `/uuf debuffs above` or the *Debuffs* switch in the window — for frames kept right above the action bars. In `modern` both rows then hang above the frame, the debuffs outermost, and under the player only the cast bar and the pet are left; in `classic` the debuffs move next to the frame, over the buffs. The frames keep their places — unless one sits so close to the top of the screen that its taller stack no longer fits — and the party column keeps its row of debuffs under each member, since it has no buffs to stand over.

`/uuf` on its own opens the options window. It is also in the addon compartment under the minimap on Retail and Forever, on a minimap button on the Classic clients, and under *Options › AddOns* on all of them. The window speaks German on a German client and English on every other; what `/uuf` prints in chat stays English, like the words it takes. Every setting in it takes effect where you stand — no `/reload`:

![The options window: a layout switch, a switch for the debuffs' place, a health bar switch, a switch for where the level stands, a theme switch, two checkboxes for Blizzard's own frames, one for the minimap button, and the unlock and reset buttons; below it, the same window in combat with the mover refused, and in the Forever theme's colors as the other clients draw it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/options-window.svg)

**The first login asks.** On an install that has never run, a window walks through the same settings one question to a page, each with a drawing of what the answer does: the layout, the health bar's color, where the level stands, whether Blizzard's own buffs and group manager stay, and how to drag the frames into place. Every answer takes effect as it is clicked, so leaving halfway loses nothing; *Skip* keeps the defaults, and `/uuf setup` brings the questions back. An update from an earlier version does not ask — its settings are already chosen.

![The onboarding: five pages, one question each. The first asks for the layout over a miniature of the screen; the others ask for the health bar's color and the level's place over a drawing of the player frame, whether Blizzard's buffs and group manager stay, and end on where everything can be found again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/onboarding.svg)

The options window offers nothing the commands do not, and `/uuf help` lists them:

| Command | Values | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/uuf` | — | the options window |
| `/uuf help` | — | this list |
| `/uuf layout` | `classic`, `modern` | the whole arrangement |
| `/uuf debuffs` | `below`, `above` | whether the debuff row goes under the buff row or over it |
| `/uuf auras` | `umbra`, `both` | who shows your buffs and debuffs |
| `/uuf health` | `class`, `plain` | what colors the health bars |
| `/uuf group` | `umbra`, `both` | whether the game's group manager stays on the left edge |
| `/uuf level` | `portrait`, `name`, `off` | where the level stands, or whether it does |
| `/uuf theme` | `auto`, `umbra`, `forever` | the frames' colors; `auto` follows the client |
| `/uuf unlock` | — | drag the frames, every one of them, filled out |
| `/uuf lock` | — | put them back to work |
| `/uuf reset` | — | forget this set's dragged positions |
| `/uuf setup` | — | the questions of the first login, again |
| `/uuf dev` | — | measurements and diagnostics, listed behind that word |

Given without a value, each setting prints what it is on and what the alternatives mean. The defaults are `modern`, `below`, `both`, `plain`, `both`, `portrait` and `auto`: Blizzard's own aura display and group panel stay up until you say otherwise, because the panel carries the raid markers and the way out of a group, and `auto` gives WoW: Forever its own look and every other client Umbra's.

Switching Blizzard's frames off in combat is a promise rather than a result — those frames are protected — and the reply says so when that happens. A layout or a debuffs placement picked in a fight is kept the same way and applied when it ends. A theme should be a result in a fight as well as out of one — it changes colors, and the client protects none of them — but no switch has been tried in one yet.

### Measurements

`/uuf dev` lists what this addon can ask the client it is running on. They report, they change nothing, and they are what a good bug report is made of:

| Command | What it answers |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/uuf dev test` | fills every aura slot with stand-ins, so a layout can be judged full, and shows the rest indicator and a raid marker on every frame — run it again to stop |
| `/uuf dev check` | which unit values this client hides, which theme and aura duration format are in force, which art the rest indicator was given, what the game answers for the target's raid marker, whether a pet's mood can be told, and how many models each portrait has loaded |
| `/uuf dev header` | whether a secure group header works on this client |
| `/uuf dev party` | what the party column is made of, child by child |
| `/uuf dev portrait` | four ways of asking what the portrait column has to draw, side by side |
| `/uuf dev debug` | what the build refused |

`check`, `header` and `party` answer in a window you can copy out of, and `portrait` in a window of squares whose screenshot is the report; `test` and `debug` write to chat. `check` also has a **key binding** under *AddOns*, for the case where the chat frame is what has gone wrong.

## Installing

The addon folder is named `UmbraUnitFrames` and the slash command is `/uuf`. An unrelated addon named *Umbra* already exists; the longer name keeps both installable side by side.

### From a release

Take the `UmbraUnitFrames` zip from [the latest release](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/releases/latest) and unpack it into `Interface\AddOns` — `_retail_\Interface\AddOns` for Retail, `_forever_\Interface\AddOns` for WoW: Forever, `_classic_\Interface\AddOns` for Mists of Pandaria Classic, `_anniversary_\Interface\AddOns` for the Anniversary realms, `_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns` for Classic Era.

One package carries every TOC file rather than one build per flavor, and the release publishes a `release.json` next to it that an addon manager reads to pick for itself.

### Running from a checkout

Copying the clone directly into `AddOns` does not work, and it fails silently: the addon simply never appears in the list. Two things differ from a released build.

1. **The folder must be named `UmbraUnitFrames`.** WoW looks for `Foo_Mainline.toc` only inside a folder named `Foo`, so a clone directory named `umbra-unit-frames` is never inspected.
2. **`Libs/oUF` is not in the repository.** It is fetched at build time and ignored by git, so a checkout has to provide it.

`tools/install.ps1` handles both. Pass the WoW path once; it is remembered afterwards.

```powershell
.\tools\install.ps1 -WowPath "C:\Games\World of Warcraft"
```

```powershell
.\tools\install.ps1 -Flavor forever
```

```powershell
.\tools\install.ps1 -Flavor mists
.\tools\install.ps1 -Flavor anniversary
.\tools\install.ps1 -Flavor era
```

Without `-Flavor` it installs for Retail.

Re-run it after every change, then `/reload` in the client. Adding the folder for the first time needs a full client restart, because the addon list is only read at launch.

## Supported clients

Umbra runs on **five clients**: Retail, WoW: Forever, and the three Classic clients — Mists of Pandaria, the Anniversary realms (Burning Crusade) and Classic Era. All five are one codebase with one copy of oUF. Code is written against the Retail API: Forever runs the Mainline UI architecture on Vanilla content, and the Classic clients, although they report themselves as Classic, carry almost all of the Midnight API. What each one lacks lives in `Compat/Forever.lua` or `Compat/Classic.lua`.

| | Retail (Midnight) | WoW: Forever | Mists of Pandaria Classic | Anniversary (Burning Crusade) | Classic Era |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Interface | `120105`, `120107` | `16001` | `50504` | `20506` | `11509` |
| `WOW_PROJECT_ID` | Mainline | Camelot (18) | Mists Classic | Burning Crusade Classic | Classic |
| API surface | 12.1.5 | 12.1.5, minus parts | 12.x, minus six things | the same as Mists | the same as Mists |
| Secret Values | yes | yes | the API is there | the API is there | the API is there |
| TOC suffix | `_Mainline` | `_Camelot` | `_Mists` | `_TBC` | `_Vanilla` |
| Umbra support | yes — verified inside an instance; 0.9's changes seen in the open world only | yes — frames, auras, portraits and the party column seen working, not yet inside an instance | frames, auras and portraits seen working, the header solo | frames, auras and portraits seen working | frames, auras and portraits seen working |

### Retail

The client everything is measured against, and verified inside an instance, where Secret Values apply.

### WoW: Forever

Forever launched on **4 November 2026**, and Umbra loads and draws on its release client as it did on the beta. The old Classic globals — `UnitAura`, `GetSpellInfo`, `GetItemInfo`, `CombatLogGetCurrentEventInfo` — do not exist there; the handful of deviations from Retail live in `Compat/Forever.lua`. One thing did not work on the beta, and it was the client's; on the release client it works.

Since build 1.60.1.70170 Forever reports a project of its own, `WOW_PROJECT_CAMELOT`, where it used to report Mainline. Umbra knows both answers from 0.8 on; before that, `/uuf` named the client unsupported and `Compat/Forever.lua` did not run. Nothing broke, but nothing on the client was told it was Forever either.

**On the beta the party column could not be built**, and the reason was below every addon: that client compiled each secure snippet with `loadstring_untainted`, its own copy of the function was missing, and the client's group-header code uses it to configure every child it creates. So the header made buttons it could not finish — no unit, no style — by oUF or by anyone else.

Umbra noticed and stepped back: two seconds after its column appears it checks whether any child was given a unit, and if none was, it hides itself, stops asking the client, and hands Blizzard's group panel back whatever `/uuf group` says. Everything else — the single frames, auras, cast bars, portraits — was unaffected. That check still runs on every client.

**On the release client it works.** Build 70009 changed the order in which the client clears that function for addons and its restricted environment takes its own copy, which is what the oUF maintainers pointed to as the fix; whether that build or a later one did it, nothing here can tell. On 8 November 2026 `/uuf dev header` built and configured a child there, as it does on Retail, and in a real group the column drew the party, the question mark of a member who had gone offline included. Nothing in Umbra had to change for it: the step back measures the header every time, so one that works is simply used.

No second party column out of fixed frames was built for the beta — it would have meant no sorting, no changes during a fight, and a second implementation to maintain — and the release client shows it was not needed. `/uuf dev header` answers where any given client stands.

**Forever's own look.** On Forever the frames wear the client's colors rather than Umbra's slate and teal: near-black plates, a one-pixel line of bronze along the top, right and bottom of each frame body, and an amber cast bar; the options window and the first-login window wear the client's own window frame, with its bronze metal, red buttons and dropdown fields. The values were sampled on 7 November 2026 off lossless screenshots of the client's own tooltip and zone plaque. The left side of each frame stays the class edge's, and nothing that belongs to the unit changes color. That is `/uuf theme auto`, the default, which picks by client; `/uuf theme umbra` keeps the slate and teal on Forever, and `/uuf theme forever` brings the bronze to any other client, where the two windows take a gold title inside a bronze border instead of Forever's frame.

![The player frame with its pet and the target with its target of target, twice over: once in Umbra's own slate and teal, and once in the Forever theme, on near-black plates with a one-pixel bronze line along the top, right and bottom of each frame body and an amber cast bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/design/forever.svg)

![The options window and the first-login window on WoW: Forever, as the game shows them: each in the game's own bronze window frame around a rock ground, with a gold title in a dark title strip and a red close button; the switches in the game's dropdown fields, gold checkboxes and red buttons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/main/assets/screenshots/forever-windows.png)

What the beta client did with Umbra, and what the release client has shown since — which values it hides, which events it is missing, how the theme and the aura timers measured — is written down in the [development notes](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/blob/main/docs/development.md).

### The Classic clients

Mists (build 5.5.4.69934), the Anniversary realms (2.5.6.69795) and Classic Era (1.15.9.69722) were each checked against the API documentation their build ships with, then played with. All three came back with the same four gaps, and a reading of Blizzard's code in October found two more that oUF reaches unguarded, so one file, `Compat/Classic.lua`, answers them for all three:

- **The aura container.** oUF builds its aura rows from the client's `AuraContainer` widget, and the Classic clients have neither that widget nor `AddDispelTypeTexture`. Where the client refuses a container, Umbra builds the row itself from plain buttons, cut by the same function and packed by the same arithmetic. The dispel color on the underline, the countdown and right-click to cancel a buff are done in Lua on those rows; canceling works out of combat only.
- **`GetUnitChargedPowerPoints`**, which oUF reads combo points through. `Compat/Classic.lua` answers nil, as Retail does for a unit without charged points.
- **`UNIT_POWER_POINT_CHARGE`**, the event oUF's class power asks for. It is left unregistered instead of being reported on every login.
- **`SetRolesets`**, a widget method oUF calls on every frame it builds. Rolesets are Midnight's rules for what an addon may do to a frame, and oUF also hides Blizzard's own frames through one. `Compat/Classic.lua` adds the method: for Umbra's frames it does nothing, and for Blizzard's it hides them the way oUF did before Midnight.
- **`PlayerVehicleHasComboPoints`**, which oUF's class power calls in a vehicle seat. Mists has vehicles and not this function, so getting in would throw; `Compat/Classic.lua` answers from the vehicle's power type.
- **`TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED`**, valid on all three, but oUF answers it through `C_ClassTalents`, which none of them has. It is left unregistered there.

The secure group header uses the same machinery as on Retail, and unlike the Forever beta it finishes its children: `/uuf dev header` built and configured one on Mists, solo. A real party is the next thing to watch it with.

What each client has no use for, or oUF does not know about, simply stays empty:

- **Mists** — Eclipse, Shadow Orbs, Burning Embers and Demonic Fury are not shown. Chi appears for Windwalker only, which is how oUF reads a Retail monk. Whether combo points arrive, when Mists keeps them on the target, is the first thing to look at.
- **Anniversary** — the boss column, and every class power but combo points.
- **Classic Era** — every class power but combo points.

### What Secret Values change

Since patch 12.0 the client returns opaque values for health, power and aura data inside encounters, Mythic+ runs and PvP matches. An addon may hand such a value to the client for display, but may not read it, compare it, or calculate with it.

This suits Umbra's design better than most: a neutral health bar with class color at the edge never needs to derive a color from a health value, so the bar looks and behaves the same inside an encounter as outside one. Two consequences are visible to you:

- **Health reads as a percentage.** The number itself is not lost—the client can still render a hidden value—but nothing may be *derived* from it. Custom thresholds, or a bar color that shifts as health drops, are not possible while the value is hidden.
- **Auras are drawn through Blizzard's aura containers** on Retail and Forever, which constrains how freely icons can be arranged. The Classic clients have no such container, so there Umbra draws the same buttons itself.

`/uuf dev check` prints which of these values the client is hiding right now, which is how any of it gets decided rather than assumed.

## Contributing

Feedback, bug reports, and focused improvements are welcome. It is especially helpful to explain **which information a change makes easier to read or understand**.

A bug report should identify the affected frame, selected layout, version, and steps to reproduce the issue — `/uuf dev check` and `/uuf dev party` give you most of that in a window you can copy out of.

The sheets in `assets/design/` are generated rather than drawn by hand — `python tools/mockups.py` rebuilds all eight. That file keeps its own copy of the metrics, so a number changed in `Core/Defaults.lua` has to be changed there too, or the sheets quietly start claiming something the addon no longer does.

The [development notes](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/blob/main/docs/development.md) are where the reasoning lives: what the client actually does, what is built, and what comes next. Please discuss larger changes in an [issue](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/issues) first, and document the source and licensing of any code or assets you contribute.

Umbra is free and stays free — nothing here is held back for sponsors. If it earns a place in your interface and you would like to support the work anyway, [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/krebs3r) is the only channel set up for it.

The inspiration is visual only. ShadowedUnitFrames carries no license file, which means no permission to reuse its code has been granted—so none of it is used here, and none of it may be contributed.

Umbra is built on [oUF](https://github.com/oUF-wow/oUF) (MIT), which is embedded at build time rather than checked in.

## License

Umbra's own code is [MIT licensed](https://github.com/krebs3r/umbra-unit-frames/blob/main/LICENSE). If this project ever goes quiet, someone else can pick it up—which is precisely what ShadowedUnitFrames could not offer.

## 0.12.1 — 16 November 2026

The target's health bar goes gray only when the kill really gives no
experience. On WoW: Forever it went gray over a level 19 target for a
level 25 hunter, and the kill still gave experience.

- The gray came from the level alone, measured against the range a quest
  goes gray in, which on Forever is narrower than the one a creature stops
  giving experience in. On Retail and Forever the level plate and the gray
  bar now ask the game about the creature itself, the way Blizzard's own
  target frame colors its level there. Mists, the Anniversary realms and
  Classic Era have no such question and keep the level's color, as their
  own target frame does
- `/uuf dev check` prints the target's difficulty both ways, with the two
  levels and whether the bar is gray
- Seen in the game on WoW: Forever: the level 19 target of the report reads
  its level green for the level 25 hunter, and its bar keeps its own color.
  Checked by eye; not yet seen on Retail

## 0.12 — 15 November 2026

Every frame shows the raid marker the game's menu puts on a unit — the
skull, the cross and the six others.

- In the top left corner of the portrait, a little in from its edges and
  inside the frame, so the target's target above the target and the buffs
  above the frames stay where they are. 16 units on the player and the
  target, clear of the rest Z's in the other corner, and 14 on the pet, the
  target's target, the party and the boss column
- The game's own art, on all five clients. The boss column shows the kill
  order the group leader marked, and a party member out of range fades with
  their marker
- Retail and WoW: Forever document the marker as a value the game may hide.
  Where it does, the marker is handed to the game untested, and if the game
  refuses it the frame shows nothing rather than an error. Not yet seen in
  a fight there; `/uuf dev check` prints what the game answered for the
  target
- Unlocking the frames and `/uuf dev test` put a marker on every frame, so
  where it sits can be seen without a group
- Seen in the game on WoW: Forever: a skull on a real target, and the
  preview on every frame. The first build sat on the frame's top line and
  was moved in; the one released was checked by eye, not yet measured. Not
  yet seen on Retail, Mists, the Anniversary realms or Classic Era

## 0.11 — 13 November 2026

The player frame shows when you are in a rest area, the way the game's own
frame does, the pet frame shows its level, and a hunter's pet shows how it
is in the color of its portrait and edge.

- In an inn or a city the game's Z's rise in the top right corner of the
  player's portrait, inside the frame, so the buffs above it and the pet in
  the other set stay where they are. They go in a fight, as on Forever's own
  frame, and come back after it
- The Z's are the game's own animation on Retail and WoW: Forever. Mists,
  the Anniversary realms and Classic Era do not have it, and show the still
  icon their own frame shows; `/uuf dev check` says which and why
- A hunter's pet frame shows the pet's mood in color: its edge and the
  portrait's ground behind the model turn green while it is happy, yellow
  while it is content — time to feed it — and red while it is unhappy. The
  pet itself is not colored over. On WoW: Forever, the Anniversary realms
  and Classic Era
- Pointing at the frame adds the game's own lines under its tooltip: the
  mood, the damage it does for it, whether its loyalty is rising or
  falling, and what it eats, in the game's language
- A warlock's demon and every pet on Retail and Mists look as they did, and
  the health bar stays green. A face like the game's own was tried twice in
  the game, at the end of the name row and beside the frame, and left out
- The pet frame shows its level, wherever `/uuf level` and the options put
  the player's: on the portrait, before the name, or not at all
- Unlocking the frames and `/uuf dev test` show the Z's, so where they sit
  can be seen without an inn
- Seen in the game: the Z's on Retail, Forever, Mists and the Anniversary
  realms, and a happy pet's mood painted on the frame on Forever. A hunter's
  pet on the Anniversary realms and Classic Era is not yet confirmed

## 0.10 — 11 November 2026

On WoW: Forever the options window and the first-login window wear the
game's own window frame, as Soundstone's and Hourstone's windows do there.

- The bronze frame with its rock ground, a title strip with the title in the
  game's gold, and the red close button. The switches lie in the game's
  dropdown field with a thin divider between their sides, the checkboxes
  take the colors of Forever's own, and Unlock, Reset, Back, Next and
  *Unlock frames* are the game's red buttons; the onboarding's drawings sit
  in the game's inset
- Every row stays where it was, and the windows keep their size, so the
  theme switch does not move under the pointer when it changes the window
  it sits in
- Only on Forever and only under the Forever theme, `auto` included. Under
  `/uuf theme umbra` the windows are as they were, and on every other
  client `/uuf theme forever` still gives them the gold title inside a
  bronze border. A switch takes effect at once, with no `/reload`
- Where the game lacks a piece of the frame's art, that piece keeps the flat
  look
- Seen in the game on both windows and measured on lossless screenshots:
  the frame flush with the window on every side, the title in the game's
  gold, the dividers and the checkbox edges one pixel, and no row moving
  when the theme is switched with the options window open
- On the first-login window's fourth page, the drawing's labels for
  Blizzard's buffs and group manager no longer run into each other in
  German: the buffs' label stands under its row

## 0.9 — 8 November 2026

A theme: on WoW: Forever the frames now wear the client's own near-black and
bronze, and everywhere else they keep Umbra's slate and teal. Aura timers
in Umbra's own short words, the same on every client that takes them, with
the cast time in the spell name's color. And the party column works on
Forever's release client, which its beta could not build; nothing in Umbra
had to change for it.

- Under Forever's theme the plates are near-black, a one-pixel line of
  bronze runs along the top, right and bottom of every frame body, the cast
  bar is amber, the teal accent turns a pale gold, the text a warm white
  and the line under a buff a warm gray. The options window and the
  first-login window carry a gold title inside a bronze border. The left
  side of a frame stays the class edge's
- `/uuf theme auto`, `umbra` or `forever` picks it, and so does the new
  Theme switch in the options window, *Thema* on a German client
- `auto` is the default, for an install that already has settings as well:
  Forever's look on WoW: Forever, Umbra's slate and teal everywhere else. So
  on Forever the frames change color with this update; `/uuf theme umbra`
  gives them back the old ones
- A switch repaints the frames where they stand, with no `/reload`. Only
  colors change and the client protects none of them, so it should take in
  combat as well; that has not been tried in a fight yet
- Unit colors never change: the health bar, incoming healing and absorbs,
  the class and reaction colors, the resources and the line under a debuff
  are the same in both
- The theme is written from lossless screenshots of Forever's own art, and
  checked on Forever against the same kind of screenshot
- Aura durations read `25m`, `8s`, `2h`, `2d` in every language, rather
  than the client's own words. On German Forever those were `25 min` and
  ran into the timer on the next icon, and Portuguese Retail and Forever
  clients word the minute the same way; even `25 m` is wider than the
  icon. The Classic clients, where Umbra writes the timer itself, now
  print the same words
- If a client refuses the new format, its own stays, and `/uuf dev check`
  says which of the two you got. The check also names the theme in force,
  and counts each portrait's model loads since the last reload
- The cast bar's remaining time is in the spell name's color. It had been
  gray, and on the cast bar's fill it all but disappeared
- The class tint in the portrait column lies behind the model now, on the
  column's ground. It used to lie over the model as well and drew a faint
  veil of class color across every face
- A 3D portrait works its camera out again once its model has loaded, and
  when the UI scale or the resolution changes. On Forever the player's
  portrait once showed a close-up of the armor instead of the face, right
  after its model had been late. Seen once and not made to happen again, so
  this is the likely fix rather than a measured one
- A model that turns up by itself while Umbra waits for it is no longer
  loaded a second time
- On WoW: Forever the party column works. The beta's own group header
  could not finish the buttons it created, so Umbra stood the column down
  there and handed Blizzard's group panel back; the release client finishes
  them. Nothing in Umbra had to change: two seconds after the column is
  shown, every time it is, Umbra checks the header again
- Checked on Retail, Forever's release client, Mists, the Anniversary
  realms and Classic Era: the theme, both `auto` and `forever`, and the
  portraits. On Forever `/uuf dev header` built and configured a child,
  and the column drew a real group. The timers were measured inside their
  icons on Forever. Not yet inside an instance, or in a fight
